key_insight: Curvature-Scaled SAM controls gradient distortion under generalized smoothness, enabling convergence guarantees where standard SAM can cycle and unnormalized SAM can diverge.
engineering_relevance: Curvature-aware perturbations and descent steps offer a principled alternative to SAM for neural-network training beyond standard smoothness assumptions.
method: Measure relative gradient distortion caused by sharpness-aware perturbations.
Scale both perturbation and descent step using curvature upper bounds.
Prove deterministic O(1/T) rates for nonconvex stationarity and convex function gaps, plus linear convergence under the Polyak–Łojasiewicz condition.
evidence_signal: In minibatch computer-vision experiments, the (H0,H1) variant achieved the highest mean best-test accuracy in all four settings against tuned SAM and USAM with constant and cosine-annealing schedules.
watch_item: The stated convergence guarantees are deterministic; practical minibatch use also depends on choosing suitable curvature upper bounds.
paper_title: Curvature-Scaled Sharpness-Aware Minimization: Convergence Beyond Smoothness
